official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 Part F publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document F 2026 was published on 24 March 2026 for England.

official_measurement_examples.name: Future effective date
official_measurement_examples.fact: Circular 01/2026 says the new approvals generally take effect on 24 March 2027, not on the July 2026 research date.

official_measurement_examples.name: HRB effective date
official_measurement_examples.fact: For the specified higher-risk-building work, the circular states an approval date of 24 September 2027 subject to transitions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Earlier standards remain relevant
official_measurement_examples.fact: Earlier Approved Document F versions continue to apply to buildings that fall under previous regulatory standards.

official_measurement_examples.name: Night vent caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Part F FAQ says a window night-vent or night-latch is not an appropriate background-ventilation solution for replacement windows.

official_measurement_examples.name: Disclaimer caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Part F FAQ says a homeowner disclaimer to fit background ventilation later does not satisfy the Building Regulations requirement.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 user guide update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The home user guide and existing-home ventilation guide were updated on 24 March 2026 alongside Future Homes and Buildings Standards changes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part F ventilation compliance is a Building Regulations question and does not itself grant planning permission or prove parcel development capacity.
